column3: The Hebrew calls the enemies “judges”; BSB expresses their role with the verb “concede.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to a singular “it” being stored with God; BSB uses plural “these things” and makes God the active subject storing them.
The Hebrew names vengeance and recompense as belonging to God; BSB changes recompense into “I will repay.”
The Hebrew uses “hand” for the failing strength; BSB says “their strength.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with a singular “let it be a shelter over you”; BSB continues with plural “let them give you shelter.”
The Hebrew repeats “I” in “I, I am He” and says “I have wounded”; BSB has one “I” and present “I wound.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the sword’s flash “lightning” and says the hand grasps judgment; BSB has “flashing sword” and says the hand grasps “it in judgment.”
The Hebrew uses singular “head” in the final phrase; BSB uses plural “heads.”

BSB adds calls for the heavens to rejoice and God’s angels to worship, and a clause about repaying those who hate Him; these clauses are absent from the Hebrew here. The Hebrew says “His servants,” where BSB has “His children.”
The Hebrew explicitly says Moses spoke “in the ears” of the people; BSB says “in the hearing” of the people.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular “word” and “it”; BSB uses plural “words” and “they.”
The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “said.”
The Hebrew calls Abarim “this mountain”; BSB says “the Abarim Range.”
The Hebrew begins with commands to die and be gathered; BSB expresses these as future events, “you will die and be gathered.”
The Hebrew repeats “among the sons of Israel”; BSB has “among the Israelites” and then “in their presence.”
The Hebrew repeats “the land”; BSB names it once and uses “it” for the other reference.
